intended_object: Per its docstring, this is the singular n-chain on the model cube Iⁿ that the comparison map `cubicalToSingular` (built by acyclic models) assigns to the identity cube of Iⁿ. It is a named intermediate term used in proofs about that comparison map.
explanation: The body does what the docstring says. It applies the degree-n component of `cubicalToSingular` at the model `cubeModel n` to the normalized chain of the identity cube `upCube n`. In the acyclic-models argument, this "image of the universal generator" fixes the whole natural chain map. Still, it is not a notion one would find defined in the literature. It is one specific chain that depends on the choices made inside the acyclic-models construction. The library uses it, together with `cubicalToSingularSubcube`, only as shorthand in lemmas about naturality and boundaries (for example `singularChains_d_cubicalToSingularGen`). So it is an auxiliary device for proofs, not a mathematical object to compare against a standard definition. Taken as such a device, it is defined correctly, and nothing in it is restricted beyond the generality of the surrounding construction (any ring `k`).
